examples.solution_text:
The interior opposite angles are $\angle BAC$ and $\angle ABC$, labelled $p$ and $q$. They are at the other two vertices.

$p+q=r$

The exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles.

$\begin{aligned}z&=58^{\circ}+67^{\circ}\\&=125^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Write an exterior-angle equation, then subtract the known interior angle.

$\begin{aligned}k+73^{\circ}&=132^{\circ}\\k&=132^{\circ}-73^{\circ}\\k&=59^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

(a) Angles opposite equal sides are equal, so $x=62^{\circ}$.

Using the exterior angle theorem:

$\begin{aligned}z&=62^{\circ}+62^{\circ}\\&=124^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

(b) Angles opposite equal sides are equal. Their sum is the exterior angle.

$\begin{aligned}x+x&=118^{\circ}\\2x&=118^{\circ}\\x&=59^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
In each case, use the exterior angle theorem to find $x$.

(a) The interior opposite angles are $52^{\circ}$ and $79^{\circ}$. The exterior angle is $(3x+5)^{\circ}$.

(b) The interior opposite angles are $(2x+12)^{\circ}$ and $(x+24)^{\circ}$. The exterior angle is $(5x-8)^{\circ}$.

(c) The exterior angle at $C$ of $\triangle ABC$ is $144^{\circ}$, and $\angle BAC$ is three times $\angle ABC$. Find $\angle ABC$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The exterior angle equals the sum of the interior opposite angles.

$\begin{aligned}3x+5&=52+79\\3x+5&=131\\3x&=126\\x&=42\end{aligned}$

(b) Write the equation, simplify and solve.

$\begin{aligned}5x-8&=(2x+12)+(x+24)\\5x-8&=3x+36\\2x&=44\\x&=22\end{aligned}$

(c) Let $\angle ABC=x^{\circ}$. Then $\angle BAC=3x^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}3x+x&=144\\4x&=144\\x&=36\end{aligned}$

$\angle ABC=36^{\circ}$.

The angle sum of $\triangle ABC$ gives

$\angle ACB=180^{\circ}-u-v$.

Angles on the straight line $ACD$ give

$\begin{aligned}w&=180^{\circ}-\angle ACB\\w&=180^{\circ}-(180^{\circ}-u-v)\\w&=u+v\end{aligned}$

By the exterior angle theorem:

$\begin{aligned}\angle QPR+40^{\circ}&=110^{\circ}\\\angle QPR&=70^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Angles on the straight line $PQS$ give

$\begin{aligned}\angle PQR&=180^{\circ}-110^{\circ}\\&=70^{\circ}\end{aligned}$.

Since $\angle QPR=\angle PQR$, their opposite sides are equal. Therefore $\triangle PQR$ is isosceles.

coverage.summary: Removed the unsupported title key from all seven candidate examples. Repaired example 3 by retaining its original case and adding a second case with equal-side markings, two unknown equal interior opposite angles and a given exterior angle of 118 degrees; the solution shows x+x=118 degrees, 2x=118 degrees and x=59 degrees. Reviewed all seven examples against the supplied source text and relevant attached images, checked their calculations and method mappings, and confirmed coverage of the distinct retained assessment methods. Checked authored gutters, diagram labels, equal-side markings and separation of givens from answers. No bare opening expression requires a phantom equals gutter. Solution prose and mathematics inherit the supplied renderer's blue styling; diagrams retain black ink and authored 10 pt labels. Baseline existing examples are empty. Actual rendered layout and final-size label verification remain for the coordinator's capture stage.

examples.derivation: The exterior angle is at C, so the opposite interior angles are BAC and ABC. Their labels are p and q; therefore p+q=r. This follows the source equation-writing examples.
The two interior opposite angles are 58° and 67°. The exterior angle is z=58°+67°=125°. The diagram places z beyond the extended side.
The exterior-angle equation is k+73°=132°. Subtracting 73° gives k=59°. The adjacent interior angle is 48°, confirming a triangle angle sum of 180°.

The ticks mark the bottom and right sides equal, so the left and top angles are equal. In (a), x=62° and z=62°+62°=124°. In (b), x+x=118°, giving x=59°. Both cases follow the source's equal-side and exterior-angle tasks; the diagrams explicitly state that they are not to scale.

In (a), 3x+5=52+79=131, so x=42. In (b), 5x-8=3x+36, so 2x=44 and x=22; the interior opposite angles are 56° and 46°, summing to the exterior angle 102°. In (c), 3x+x=144, so x=36 and angle ABC=36°. These use the retained assessed equation-solving method without introducing a further skill.
Triangle angle sum gives angle ACB=180°-u-v. Since A, C and D are collinear, w=180°-angle ACB=180°-(180°-u-v)=u+v. This independently reproduces the source's angle-sum and straight-line proof.

The exterior angle gives angle QPR=110°-40°=70°. The straight line PQS gives angle PQR=180°-110°=70°. Equal angles at P and Q imply equal opposite sides QR and PR, so triangle PQR is isosceles, following source Mastery question 10b.
